item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I like how this story makes reference to historical events, although I am not sure if that's intended by the writer or not. The first battle was probably the Campaign at the China–Burma border in 1960. In that battle, the PLA marched into Burma to engage a Nationalist remnant force based in there under acquiescence from the Burmaese. It matchs the timeframe (the 'Great Leap Forward' campaign) and the tropical scenery described in the tale.

I'm not sure about the second battle, but it seems to base on the many island campaigns fought between the PRC and ROC during the early 50s.

item.title: Meh
item.content:encoded: While it's plausible that she was created, as necessitated by the story, and despite the ridiculousness of this particular iteration of the "supersoldier" concept (even compared to most iterations), it's more than a little laughable that such a manifestation of the idea would present any sort of efficacy whatsoever to anyone with a firearm and more than about 5 meters of clearance between themselves and their target.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The language here is a little weak. There are some places here I feel you could've been very vivid with to drive it home.

Blood gushed out.

This here is one. Later on you say 'until I could feel nothing except the blood in my mouth.' which is pretty nice.

They put me on a beach. They pointed towards the "enemy."

I saw no enemies. Only scared men and boys.

This is nice, but the rest of it is very minimalist, to the point where it's hard to discern what's going on, the setting, the context, etc. It's abstract actions floating in a plane of unknowns.

The last part is pretty neat, but everything else is so barebones it's hard to know what's happening.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really like the way this turned out. The stream of consciousness really gets you inside her mind to watch her break slowly. I might have done with a little more gruesomeness just to hammer the point home, but how it was executed here is quite good. I like that she wants to be not what she is. I like that she's willing to permanently deafen herself to keep herself from killing again. I know articles like 326 usually include feels of this nature already, but I would love to see more things done with this sort of theme. Skips are people too, even non-human ones, and it's a shame that this avenue is so seldom explored.

+1. My only real gripe is that the imagery could have been more vivid, but I still really like this.

item.title: Overview/Description
item.content:encoded:
This story is about SCP-326, and it's sort of an origin story. Credit goes to Voct for rewriting the original 326 from a Chinese Anime Murder Cyborg into a sad old lady, and for describing the eardrum-destroying scene so vividly that I knew I had to write the story. And also for fixing my dialogue tags. (They were pretty damn awful.)

Again, thank you, Voct, for letting me use one of your SCP's in my very first tale (and the first thing I posted to the main site)

EDIT: I forgot to mention that there are two history easter eggs in here as well.
